scope.flow: GaugeV2 time-based lock-up: deposit and immediate withdrawal in the same transaction/block
scope.environment: Not specified beyond a block.timestamp-based Solidity contract

statements.text: The maturityTime mapping is never initialized or updated anywhere in the contract and uninitialized uint256 mapping keys default to 0.
block.timestamp is always greater than 0 in any real-world scenario.
_withdraw contains a maturity check requiring block.timestamp >= maturityTime[msg.sender] before a user can withdraw.
The user holds tokens deposited in GaugeV2 before attempting the withdrawal.
A user can call the GaugeV2 deposit and withdraw functions.
The user deposits tokens into GaugeV2.
The user calls _withdraw to withdraw the tokens in the same transaction or block.
Because maturityTime[msg.sender] is 0 while block.timestamp is greater than 0, the condition block.timestamp >= maturityTime[msg.sender] always evaluates to true, making the maturity check a no-op.
The user completes a withdrawal in the same transaction or block as the deposit, bypassing the intended lock-up period.
Tokens deposited just before reward distribution could be claimed and immediately withdrawn with no lock-up penalty, enabling flash-staking against the reward system.
A user's withdrawal from GaugeV2 should only complete once block.timestamp >= maturityTime[msg.sender], enforcing the intended time-based lock-up before the user's stake can be withdrawn.
The maturityTime value for a user was intended to be recorded at deposit time, marking the end of the lock-up period.

ambiguities: The point/source where maturityTime is set is not reported; deposit-time setting is only inferred.
Access control on deposit and _withdraw beyond users moving their own tokens is not specified.
Whether withdrawal requires an existing positive deposited balance is not explicitly stated.
Flash-staking reward claim and resulting profit are described only as potential, not independently asserted.
block.timestamp greater than 0 is asserted only for real-world scenarios, not proven for all chains.
